messages:
Carmen S: FYI - multiple EU-1 customers reporting p99 spikes / timeouts on /v1/generate for OrionX v2 when input >12k tokens. Getting escalations from support.
Ben R: Which pool/region and when did this land? Any config flips recently? :eyes: 
Carmen S: EU-1 dedicated pool. Deploy happened 2026-03-16T22:10:02Z. During onboarding we flipped tokenizer flag `merge-units-v3=true` for the model. Attaching a sanitized customer log: 
```
2026-03-16T22:13:11Z request_id=xyz789 stage=tokenize time=8.9s seq_len=12456
2026-03-16T22:13:11Z stage=decode time=0.12s kv_cache_miss=false
2026-03-16T22:13:11Z total_server_time=11.1s p99 threshold breach
```
Maya P: Confirmed metric bump - prior p99 for longctx was ~600ms, current shows ~2.8s across affected routes.
infra-bot: Deploy event: model_onboard/orionx:v2 by release-bot at 2026-03-16T22:10:02Z. Flags: {"merge-units-v3": true}.
Ben R: Can we repro? Need a curl to hit long-context path and a single failing request id to trace. I'll try a replica in EU-1.
Carmen S: Repro steps from the customer case: 1) system + ~11.5k token document; 2) POST /v1/generate model=orionx:v2 stream=false; 3) observe tail p99 >10s in some attempts. Their curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"orionx:v2","input":"<~11.5k tokens>","max_tokens":100}'
```
Jasper L: tagging @eng-runtime @eng-ml - my quick read: new tokenizer heuristic probably scans more aggressively and can trigger pathological behavior (regex/backtracking or quadratic scanning) on large docs. That would explain big tokenize time. Also could be boundary handling causing extra passes.
Alice K: If KV cache were invalidated we'd see higher decode times; decode is small here so this is tokenizer-bound. Need proxy-level timing for a single request_id for confirmation. Carmen, can you paste the full proxy trace for xyz789?
Carmen S: Proxy trace (sanitized): 
```
proxy.recv 0.006s
router.match 0.011s
tokenizer.exec 8.90s
worker.queue 0.003s
runtime.decode 0.12s
response.flush 0.02s
```
Ben R: tokenizer.exec ~9s - that nails it. Short-term mitigations: (A) rollback the tokenizer flag for orionx:v2, (B) route affected customers to orionx:v1, or (C) enable server-side input-chunking feature (if safe for customer semantics). Which is fastest?
Maya P: I've applied a routing override to pin the three impacted accounts to orionx:v1 as emergency mitigation (acct-112, acct-998, acct-210). Support confirmed p99 dropped back to ~650-800ms within 8 minutes. Support Bot logged action.
Support Bot: Action logged - routing override applied for accounts [acct-112, acct-998, acct-210]. Owner: Maya P.
Jasper L: That validates tokenizer flag as root cause. Next steps: eng-ml to run tokenizer microbench on 12k+ inputs comparing merge-units-v3 vs previous algorithm and profile hotspots. eng-runtime to add a fast-fail / circuit-breaker when tokenizer.exec > 2s to prevent tail amplification. Also add telemetry for token_count and tokenizer_time per request.
Alice K: For long-term, we should avoid defaulting users to the new heuristic until it's validated at scale. Eng-ml - can you produce an optimized patch or revert implementation detail that kept the semantics but improves scanning?
Maya P: Scheduling postmortem with eng-ml + eng-runtime tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Created ticket INF-4829 and assigned owners.
Jasper L: I'll open a small routing/flag rollback PR and a CI regression that runs a 12k token file through the tokenizer under both flags and asserts tokenize <1s. PR will be posted to track.
Support Bot: Thread status changed: triaged -> in_progress.
Carmen S: Customer updated: we pinned them to previous model and will follow up after eng teams investigate. Customer accepted the temporary workaround. Closing loop in INF-4829 with graphs and request ids.
Ben R: Action list: (1) eng-ml run microbench + flamegraph (due 48h); (2) eng-runtime add tokenizer timeout/circuit-breaker + telemetry (due 24h); (3) support monitor pinned accounts and confirm no regressions (ongoing). Owner: Jasper L.
Jasper L: I'll post PR link here once available (https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5421).
